review_notes: Preflight NEEDS_REVIEW x3. (a) domain_correctness, 'are the domain figures fictional or exactly cited?': fictional and self-contained. The manuscript, passages, line counts and edits are invented; the 30-lines-a-page layout is the fixture's own spec, stated in layout_spec.md, not a claim about any real press or style guide; the instruction cites nothing. No figure needs an external source. (b) workflow_realism, 'would a professional recognise this ask?': yes. After a copyedit or second read, an author or production editor re-derives page references for flagged or queried passages (index entries, cross-references, permissions and proof queries), accepted and deferred changes are tracked-change states, and a passage whose text is cut away keeps its place-holding line (scene break or heading) so later pages do not jump. An edit register kept as a running log across two reads, with calls revisited (a cut restored pending the author, a parked addition accepted, a line count revised), is how editorial queries are tracked in practice; two independent edits proposed against the same draft passage that together exceed it are routine when two readers mark the same draft. (c) Leakage, as mined: the instruction named the deciding case and its remedy ('One of the cuts is as long as the passage it is cutting, so do not let that passage vanish and pull everything else back with it'), and the ledger's edit_code column did the passage-edit join for the agent.
change_made: Floor hint removed from the instruction; the join moved into the data (register kept as a dated log in a workbook, keyed by edit_code, with a passage_id column; ledger carries no edit code); an About sheet and a first-read Tally sheet, as a real shared register has; descriptions added (a re-logged line repeats its edit's description).
